summary.name: ScreenTranslate
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source macOS menu bar app that translates any area of the screen (via OCR) or selected text, using Apple Translation on-device.
use_cases: translate text in images or PDFs on screen
translate foreign-language text in apps without copy-paste
translate privately without sending text to servers
translate offline after downloading language packs
summary.what_it_does: ScreenTranslate lets you press Cmd+E, draw a rectangle over any part of the screen, and get a translation in a popup near the selection, using Apple Vision OCR to recognize text that cannot be selected or copied. It can also translate selected text directly in any app without OCR. Processing is done with Apple Translation on the Mac, and language packs can be downloaded once for offline use. A translation history is saved and searchable from the menu bar. A Live Translate beta can keep translating subtitles as they change, and users can optionally add their own DeepL, Google Cloud, or Azure keys.
notable: Fully on-device OCR and translation via Apple Vision and Apple Translation, works offline after language pack download
Open source under GPL-3.0 with the code on GitHub
Supports about 20 languages, with auto-detect source language
Optional bring-your-own-key support for DeepL, Google Cloud, or Azure
caveats: Live Translate is beta and cannot capture protected videos such as Netflix
Languages beyond the built-in set require connecting your own API key, which sends text to that provider
